sec: Precautions and the delay table · p826

items.q: Match the heparin precaution chain — 1) Syringe flushed with 2) Solution used  3) Effect of excess heparin … A) ↓HCO₃⁻ and ↓PCO₂  B) 0.5 ml of 1 : 1000 heparin  C) Emptied before sampling
items.exp: Precaution: the syringe should be flushed with 0.5 ml (1 : 1000 heparin) solution and emptied; excess heparin gives a dilutional effect with ↓HCO₃⁻ and ↓PCO₂. (Book p826)

items.q: Excess heparin in the ABG syringe produces which changes?
opts: No change because heparin is chemically inert
items.exp: Excess heparin → ↑ dilutional effect → ↓HCO₃⁻ and ↓PCO₂. (Book p826)

items.q: Fill up: The sample must be transported earliest via ______.
items.exp: The sample must be transported earliest via the cold chain, since delay changes the measured values. (Book p826)

items.q: Match the change in value per 10 minutes of delay — 1) pH  2) pCO₂  3) pO₂ … A) 1 mmHg un-iced vs 0.1 mmHg iced  B) 0.01 un-iced vs 0.001 iced  C) 0.1% un-iced vs 0.01% iced
items.exp: Delay table (per 10 minutes): pH 0.01 un-iced at 37°C versus 0.001 iced at 4°C; pCO₂ 1 mmHg versus 0.1 mmHg; pO₂ 0.1% versus 0.01%. (Book p826)

items.q: How much does pH change every 10 minutes in an un-iced sample kept at 37°C?
items.exp: Un-iced sample at 37°C: pH changes by 0.01 every 10 minutes, versus 0.001 in an iced sample at 4°C. (Book p826)

items.q: In an iced sample at 4°C, the change in pH per 10 minutes is:
items.exp: Iced samples slow the change tenfold: pH 0.001, pCO₂ 0.1 mmHg and pO₂ 0.01% per 10 minutes. (Book p826)

items.q: An ABG is left at room temperature for 20 minutes and pH values are compared. What does the printed table predict?
opts: pH falls by about 0.02, along with a pCO₂ rise of about 2 mmHg
pH rises by about 0.02, along with a pCO₂ fall of about 2 mmHg
pH is unchanged because delay affects only pO₂
pH falls by 0.1 with a pO₂ rise of 1%
items.exp: At 37°C the change is 0.01 pH per 10 minutes (so ~0.02 over 20 minutes) and 1 mmHg pCO₂ per 10 minutes (~2 mmHg); the pO₂ change is 0.1% per 10 minutes. (Book p826)

items.q: ‘Icing the sample at 4°C reduces the per-10-minute change in pCO₂ to 0.1 mmHg.’
opts: True — 0.1 mmHg iced versus 1 mmHg un-iced
False — icing has no effect on pCO₂ drift
True — the iced change is 1 mmHg and the un-iced 0.1 mmHg
False — icing reduces only the pO₂ change
items.exp: Delay table: pCO₂ changes 1 mmHg per 10 minutes un-iced at 37°C but only 0.1 mmHg iced at 4°C. (Book p826)

items.q: All but one of the following are printed precautions for ABG sampling. Which is the odd one out?
opts: Store the sample at body temperature until analysis
Flush the syringe with 0.5 ml of 1 : 1000 heparin solution and empty it
Transport the sample earliest via the cold chain
Avoid excess heparin within the syringe
items.exp: The printed precautions are heparin flushing and emptying (0.5 ml of 1 : 1000), earliest transport via the cold chain, and awareness of delay-induced changes — keeping the sample at body temperature is not advised. (Book p826)
